title: Characterization of coRP with Polynomial-Time Verifiers
statement: A language $L$ belongs to coRP with polynomial-time machines if and only if its complement has a polynomial-time verifier with one-sided error: for some natural numbers $a,k$, it uses $a(|x|+1)^k$ random bits, accepts each input in the complement with probability at least $2/3$, and rejects every input outside the complement on every random string. The verifier is polynomial-time efficient in the sense that its true-output and false-output sets on encoded input-randomness pairs both lie in $P$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language over bit strings
